verdict.purpose: The answer word. Fit formula min(100cqi / (len x fit), cap); fit .435 at weight 900; cap 42svh phone, 50svh from 900px. JA! rests at 900, NEIN! at 100 (fontWeight shown is the JA! state). The '!' is red.

verdict-teaser.purpose: 'Ja?\nNein?' on two forced lines at weight 100 during suspense; --len 5, fit .44; cap 42svh phone, 25svh desktop.

headline.purpose: The question 'Hast du Eier?' in the header.

title.purpose: Answer line (dek) under the verdict; clamp(1.625rem, 2.2vw, 2.125rem) from 900px; balanced wrap.

note.purpose: Tagline (Soft Ink), friend note and toast (600, Ink).

caption.purpose: Clip credit and footer, Soft Ink.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The one easing: weight morph and button/badge state transitions.

motion.name: breathe
motion.purpose: Suspense teaser while the answer is drawn (suspense itself lasts 1400ms even under reduced motion).

motion.name: reduced-motion

opticalSideBearing.apply: margin-inline-start: calc(var(--lsb) * -1em * var(--trim)); --trim 1 on phones (flush-left), 0 from 900px (centred).

grid.areas: row 1 verdict 1-12 centred; row 2 text 1-4, actions 5-8, clip 9-12

narrative.overview:
The category standard for a one-question oracle site, played straight to a Swiss poster and Apple product page bar: a small question, one enormous word, the clip, two actions. The only idea is typographic. The verdict is set on Hanken Grotesk's variable weight axis, so JA! lands at the heaviest weight (900) and NEIN! at the thinnest (100): the word itself either has Eier or has none. Everything else on the page stays out of its way.

The page is white paper with black ink, hairline rules and a single Swiss red. Density is low and the hierarchy is extreme: the verdict is sized to fill the measure, everything beneath it is set at reading sizes in the same family. No props, no costume, no decoration; depth, texture and gradient are absent by design.

Motion is a single event per state. The thin teaser "Ja? Nein?" breathes once while the answer is drawn, then the verdict morphs its weight to the final value. Nothing else enters, slides or fades.
keyCharacteristics: One face (Hanken Grotesk variable, 100-900); hierarchy by size and weight only.
White, black ink, and one red used in exactly two places.
Verdict fitted to its container width, capped by viewport height.
Weight morph as the signature and only entrance motion.
Square corners, 1px hairline rules, no shadows.
12-column desktop grid; single column on phones with 20px margins.

rules.name: The Two Reds Rule
rules.body: Red appears exactly twice on any screen: the 6px top rule and the "!" of the verdict. The teaser ("Ja? Nein?") carries no red. A third red element breaks the system.

rules.name: The Hover Inverts Rule
rules.body: Interactive states trade ink and white; they never introduce a new hue. The one tonal step is the primary button hover (`#2b2b2b`).

rules.name: The Weight Is the Verdict Rule
rules.body: Yes is weight 900, no is weight 100, suspense is 100. Never set the verdict at a middle weight at rest, and never signal yes/no with color.

rules.name: The Fit, Not Clamp Rule
rules.body: The verdict is sized from its container width and its character count, never from a fixed clamp. A new verdict word must set `--len` and, if its weight changes, a re-measured `--fit`.

rules.name: The Optical Edge Rule
rules.body: On phones the verdict hangs flush-left with its first stem on the margin at every weight. The left side-bearing of the first glyph is a registered custom property (`--lsb`, number, em) animated alongside the weight: J measures 0.042em at 100 and 0.016em at 900; N measures 0.097em at 100 and 0.059em at 900. The verdict's inline-start margin is `-lsb × 1em × trim`, with trim 1 on phones and 0 on desktop, where the word is centred and needs no correction.

rules.name: The Answer First Rule
rules.body: While the answer is being drawn, text, clip and actions keep their space (`visibility: hidden`) so nothing shifts when the verdict lands.

rules.name: The Paper Rule
rules.body: If an element needs to stand apart, give it a hairline or white space, not a shadow or a tint.

dos: **Do** keep red to the 6px top rule and the verdict's "!".
**Do** express yes and no through weight alone: 900 for JA!, 100 for NEIN!, 100 for the teaser.
**Do** size the verdict with the fit formula and set `--len` per word; re-measure `--fit` for any new weight or word shape.
**Do** animate `--lsb` with the weight so a flush-left verdict keeps its first stem on the margin at every weight.
**Do** let the weight morph be the only entrance motion; everything else simply stands there once the answer lands.
**Do** jump to the final weight under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
**Do** separate blocks with 1px hairlines and white space on the 12-column grid.
**Do** keep all corners square and all states inside the ink/white pair.
donts: **Don't** add a second typeface; Hanken Grotesk carries every role.
**Don't** use shadows, gradients, textures or rounded corners.
**Don't** color the verdict or any state green, red or otherwise to mean yes/no.
**Don't** fade, slide or stagger in the text, clip or buttons.
**Don't** add props, illustrations or literal eggs; the type is the whole idea.
**Don't** set the verdict with a fixed clamp or let it wrap (the teaser's two-line break is the only exception).
